origin: Named after masonry, where bricks are laid in staggered rows: cards of different heights are stacked without gaps. David DeSandro's JavaScript library Masonry made the name known, and Pinterest is the best-known example.
whenToUse: Collections of ideas or recipes whose photos have different proportions.
Screens for browsing and picking what you like.
whenNotToUse: Order matters (the top-to-bottom reading order gets confusing).
Cards have similar heights (use an ordinary grid).
Items are compared in aligned rows, like a table.

alternatives.name: Image Gallery
alternatives.reason: Looking closely at photos one by one.

accessibility: CSS columns flow top to bottom within each column, so place the DOM in reading order.
Name the list so the number of items is read along with it.
Use break-inside: avoid so cards aren't split between columns.
Column count buttons announce their state with aria-pressed.
